questionText:
The value of the definite integral

$$\int_{-3}^{3} \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-1}^{1} (4x^2y - z^3) \, dz \, dy \, dx$$

is ____________ . (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
explanation:
Step 1: Split the integral into two separate terms.
The given triple integral is:
$I = \int_{-3}^{3} \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-1}^{1} (4x^2y - z^3) \, dz \, dy \, dx = I_1 - I_2$

where,
$I_1 = \int_{-3}^{3} \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-1}^{1} 4x^2y \, dz \, dy \, dx$
$I_2 = \int_{-3}^{3} \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-1}^{1} z^3 \, dz \, dy \, dx$

Step 2: Evaluate $I_1$.
Since the limits of integration are constant, we can factor the integral:
$I_1 = \left(\int_{-3}^{3} 4x^2 \, dx\right) \cdot \left(\int_{-2}^{2} y \, dy\right) \cdot \left(\int_{-1}^{1} 1 \, dz\right)$
Since $f(y) = y$ is an odd function integrated over symmetric limits $[-2, 2]$, $\int_{-2}^{2} y \, dy = 0$.
Therefore, $I_1 = 0$.

Step 3: Evaluate $I_2$.
Similarly, factoring $I_2$:
$I_2 = \left(\int_{-3}^{3} 1 \, dx\right) \cdot \left(\int_{-2}^{2} 1 \, dy\right) \cdot \left(\int_{-1}^{1} z^3 \, dz\right)$
Since $g(z) = z^3$ is an odd function integrated over symmetric limits $[-1, 1]$, $\int_{-1}^{1} z^3 \, dz = 0$.
Therefore, $I_2 = 0$.

Conclusion:
The total value is $I = 0 - 0 = 0$.
